title: 'He was not a monster': loved ones of man who died in police incident speak out
article: According to his loved ones, Joshua John Robert Megeney was a hard-working family man who struggled with addictions but did not deserve to die.
"He was not a monster. Far from it," said Sharlene van de Graaf, who's former daughter-in-law was in a relationship with Megeney for two and a half years.
Police identified Megeney, 28, as the man who died inside a house in the 500 Block of Avenue Q North after police were called there for a report of a break-and-enter in progress on Thursday.

Van de Graaf said she met Megeney when he came to Saskatoon a few months ago from his home in Medicine Hat. He and his girlfriend - van de Graaf's former daughter-in-law, with whom she is still close - were living on the streets, struggling with addiction.
"The power of addiction goes beyond reason. Try to see it from the human side," she said, speaking with other family members in a home just one block from where the standoff happened.
On Friday afternoon, police tape surrounded the scene of the incident as crews worked to clean up debris left over from the seven hours police surrounded the home.

Police have said officers fired shots after encountering a man with a long-barrelled gun inside a bedroom of the house around 9:15 a.m. Megeney's body was found there when police re-entered the home hours later, around 4:30 p.m. It's still unclear whether police shot Megeney, or how he died. For her part, van de Graaf said she justice will prevail.
"I hope they tell the truth," she said.
Megeney was from Medicine Hat and had been working on the oil rigs, van de Graaf said. That's where he met his girlfriend. The two of them eventually came to Saskatoon after Megeney lost his job.
Although he wasn't married to her mother, Kadie Lavallee said she considered Megeney her step-dad. She said she shared good memories with him spent time with him Wednesday night.
"He was nothing but a family man," she said.
Lavallee said Megeney had just been released from jail in Saskatoon and was ordered to leave the city. Since he was living on the street, he had no money, she said.
Lavallee and her grandmother said they don't know why Megeney was in the house or why he allegedly broke into it. They said he was trying to get help for his addictions.
"I just wish he had overcome his addictions," van de Graaf said.

Weighill said an investigation into the "police-related shooting" is ongoing. He said he believes two officers discharged their firearms, but could not say how many shots were fired or how Megeney died.
The home's owner kept several guns in the house, but they were locked in a gun case, according to his son.
Major crimes investigators have taken over the case and a third party oversight body is also reviewing the incident.
